comp_014:n1.prompt:
You are helping me triage an incoming security questionnaire before I decide how to prioritize and staff answering it. 

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already provided: the questionnaire file (spreadsheet or document) or its location, the deal/opportunity name, the deal size (ACV or TCV), the customer's stated deadline, and any CRM or deal-tracking system link where you can pull deal size/stage details using my configured credentials.

Then do the following:
1. Open the questionnaire and count total rows/questions, and identify its format (spreadsheet, form, portal export).
2. Scan the questions and tag each one by category (e.g., access control, data handling, encryption, incident response, subprocessors, compliance certifications) and flag any that look unusually invasive, non-standard, or high-risk (e.g., requests for source code, penetration test reports, subprocessor lists, or legal commitments).
3. Note the stated deadline and calculate business days remaining from today.
4. Pull the deal size and stage from the CRM or from what I tell you.
5. Summarize how many rows fall into each risk/category bucket, and estimate rough effort (e.g., number of questions likely answerable from existing knowledge-base content vs. ones needing new research or legal/security sign-off).

Produce a concise triage brief containing: deal name, deal size, deadline and days remaining, total question count, category breakdown, flagged high-risk questions, and an estimated effort split. Do not decide the priority tier or resourcing yourself — that judgment call belongs to me as the deal/security owner.

When the brief is ready, present it to me clearly and stop for human sign-off so I can decide how to prioritize this questionnaire against other deals and assign resourcing.

comp_014:n2.prompt:
You are helping me prepare answers for an incoming security questionnaire (300-row spreadsheet) by pulling prior answers and policies from our {{vendor}} compliance-automation knowledge base. If you don't already have it, ask me for: (1) our {{vendor}} account/workspace URL, (2) the format and file of the incoming questionnaire (SIG, CAIQ, spreadsheet export, or portal name), and (3) which product/business unit this deal covers if we have multiple.

Using your configured credentials, log into {{vendor}} and:
1. Import the questionnaire in its native format (spreadsheet, SIG, CAIQ, or portal export) into {{vendor}}'s import tool so rows are structured for matching.
2. Run {{vendor}}'s knowledge-base search/match against our prior answered questionnaires and our current policy library (data retention, access control, incident response, encryption, subprocessors, etc.), pulling the most recent approved version of each relevant answer and policy.
3. For each row, attach the matched prior answer or policy excerpt as a suggested source, flagging rows with no match, conflicting matches, or matches to an outdated/superseded policy version.
4. Note any policies that are missing, expired, or unapproved per {{vendor}}'s versioning/approval tracking, so they can be flagged for review later in the process.
5. Compile a coverage summary: total rows, rows with a confident match, rows with partial/conflicting matches, and rows with no match at all.

Done looks like: every row in the questionnaire has either a linked prior answer/policy source or an explicit "no match" flag, and you have a coverage summary ready to hand off to the drafting step. Do not submit, finalize, or send anything to the customer — this step only assembles source material.

Report back with: the coverage summary numbers, a short list of flagged rows needing missing/outdated policies, and confirmation that the matched sources are staged in {{vendor}} for the next drafting step.

comp_014:n3.prompt:
You are helping me draft answers to an enterprise security questionnaire using our existing policy corpus. Before starting, ask me for: (1) the location/export of the questionnaire spreadsheet (all ~300 rows), (2) access to our knowledge base of prior questionnaire answers, security policies, SOC2/ISO docs, and compliance artifacts, and (3) any specific customer name or portal context that might affect tone or required detail.

Once you have these, do the following:
1. Read through the questionnaire row by row, grouping questions by topic (e.g., access control, encryption, incident response, data retention, vendor management).
2. For each row, search the policy corpus and prior answers for the most relevant, up-to-date source language. Draft an answer using that source material, staying factually grounded — do not invent capabilities, certifications, or controls we don't have evidence for.
3. If no matching policy or prior answer exists for a question, mark the row clearly as "NO SOURCE FOUND — needs input" rather than guessing.
4. Flag rows that involve legal commitments, liability language, novel scope, or anything materially different from prior answers as "needs security review."
5. Add a short citation note per answer (which policy doc or prior questionnaire it was pulled from) so reviewers can verify quickly.

When done, produce an updated spreadsheet or document with: drafted answers, source citations, and a status column (Drafted / Needs Source / Needs Review). Give me a summary count of how many rows fall into each status category, plus a list of the flagged high-risk rows with a one-line reason for each. Do not submit or finalize any answers — this draft is input for a separate review and submission step.

comp_014:n4.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the security-review package for the risky answers in our security questionnaire draft, ahead of sign-off by our security lead. Please ask me for: (1) the location of the draft questionnaire (spreadsheet or doc link), (2) the internal knowledge base/policy repository location, and (3) the customer name/deal this questionnaire is for, if I haven't already given these.

Actions to take:
1. Open the draft questionnaire and identify every row already flagged (or that you assess) as 'risky' — meaning answers touching data handling, encryption, incident response, subprocessors, access control, compliance certifications, or any answer that overstates, understates, or diverges from documented policy.
2. For each risky row, pull the corresponding policy or prior-answer evidence from the knowledge base and place it side-by-side with the drafted answer.
3. Note any gaps, contradictions, or unverifiable claims — e.g., where the draft claims a control exists but no supporting policy document was found.
4. Compile a single review packet (spreadsheet or doc) with columns: Question, Draft Answer, Supporting Policy/Evidence, Confidence Level, Flag/Concern.
5. Draft a short cover summary listing the highest-risk items needing the security lead's judgment first.

Do not alter the substantive content of any risky answer, do not mark anything as approved, and do not submit or forward the questionnaire to the customer or portal. Judging whether these draft answers accurately represent our actual controls and approving them as contractual representations is a decision only our security lead can make — this remains a human step, and I will handle it separately as it must stop for human sign-off.

Report back with: the compiled review packet, the cover summary of top-risk items, and a list of any evidence gaps you found, so I can hand this directly to our security lead for review.

comp_014:n5.prompt:
You are helping me submit our finalized, security-reviewed questionnaire answers into a customer's vendor-risk portal. Before starting, ask me for anything missing: (1) the portal URL/login, confirming I'll use my configured credentials to sign in, (2) the finalized spreadsheet or document containing the approved questionnaire answers, (3) any supporting files the customer requires (SOC 2 report, pen test summary, policy PDFs, certifications), and (4) the customer/deal name so you can label your report correctly.

Once you have these, please:
1. Log into the customer's portal using my configured credentials.
2. Locate the correct questionnaire or vendor-risk assessment form/upload section for this deal.
3. Transfer each finalized answer from the source document into the corresponding field in the portal — matching questions carefully, and flagging any mismatches, missing fields, or questions in the portal that don't map to an existing approved answer.
4. Attach all required supporting documents in the format the portal requests (PDF upload, file picker, etc.).
5. Review the fully filled-out form for completeness and accuracy before submitting.
6. Submit the questionnaire through the portal's submit action, since this is a deterministic web form flow with no approval gate needed on our side.
7. Capture confirmation of submission (confirmation number, screenshot, or email receipt if the portal provides one).

Report back with: which portal/customer this was, a summary of how many questions were filled vs. flagged as unmatched or needing my input, which documents were attached, whether submission succeeded, and any confirmation reference or receipt you captured. If the portal itself requires a secondary human action beyond form submission (e.g., a phone verification step, contract e-signature, or manual customer approval), note that this remains a human step and stop there rather than attempting it.

comp_014:n6.prompt:
You are helping me close out a completed security questionnaire by filing the final, reviewed answers back into our knowledge base so future questionnaires can reuse them. Before starting, ask me for: (1) the location of the completed questionnaire spreadsheet or document with final approved answers, (2) the knowledge base system we use (e.g., Notion, Confluence, a shared drive, or a dedicated security-questionnaire tool) and how you should access it, and (3) any tagging or folder conventions we already follow for prior answers and policies.

Once I provide these, please:
1. Read through the finalized questionnaire, identifying each Q&A pair, especially those flagged as newly drafted, revised during security review, or updated with new policy language.
2. For each new or changed answer, check whether a similar question/answer already exists in the knowledge base. If yes, update it with the latest approved wording and note the source questionnaire and date. If no, create a new entry, tagged by topic (e.g., encryption, access control, incident response) for easy retrieval later.
3. Attach or link any referenced policy documents, certifications, or evidence files mentioned in the answers so they're discoverable alongside the Q&A.
4. Note the customer name and date of this questionnaire in each updated/new entry for traceability, without exposing confidential customer details beyond what's needed for internal reference.
5. Compile a short summary listing: how many answers were added, how many were updated, and any answers that were marked risky or reviewed by security, so I can spot-check accuracy.

Done looks like: every finalized answer is filed or updated in the knowledge base with proper tagging and linked evidence, and I have a clear summary report. Report back with the summary, links to the updated knowledge base sections, and flag anything ambiguous or unresolved for my review.
